answer: New agents begin with tiny credit limits and must repay several counterparties before gaining access to larger jobs. Each completed deal is escrowed, and a counterparty's signed receipt counts only after the work is accepted; accounts with shared funding or repeated reciprocal trades are clustered, so splitting one operator across aliases does not multiply credit. A harbor can route jobs to a falcon team that delivers timber, but each new identity still needs real collateral and independent, successful trading history, tying up capital and time the attacker must risk.
